name: kalshi-history-index-markets
notes: Structural gates over one markets pull of source kalshi-history-index (settled S&P 500 / Nasdaq-100 ladders from both archives). The rule set is crypto_trading's suite-kalshi-history-markets.json with the series swapped: the same pack, the same fields, so the same gates. It restates the series list on purpose (a suite must not read its expectations from the source it validates); tests/test_index_configs.py pins the two equal. Run: python -m dskit.onboarding validate --suite configs/suite-kalshi-history-index-markets.json --snapshot <snapshot-vid> --root <store root>.

rules.notes: An empty pull is a broken pull (wrong series, API change, a cutoff that moved the archive), never a quiet day.

One row per market per pull. The live copy of a market the archive also listed is dropped by the pack WHATEVER its settlement time (the real archive lists markets settled about a day after market_settled_ts, probed 2026-10-07); a duplicate here means that routing failed.
Each of the four series returned at least one settled market. Four restates the series list; the pin test keeps them equal.
The four series the sources pull, RESTATED here on purpose. tests/test_index_configs.py pins this list equal to every source config's series.

The source asks for settled markets, so every row should be final: the live API spells it 'finalized' and the archive may spell it 'settled'. Another status is a market whose result and value are not yet known: read it before modelling.

A settled market reads yes or no. '' means unsettled and anything else (void, scalar) is a settlement the calibration must handle by name: fail here so it is decided, then amend the suite (a new, auditable hash).
A value that is neither a known geometry nor empty is a new market type: block until a payoff rule exists. Empty is allowed here and WARNED by markets-strike-type-set.
An EMPTY strike_type is a market never given a strike. Index ladders set strikes at listing, so an empty one is unexpected: warn by name rather than block, as the crypto suite does.
Strikes are S&P 500 or Nasdaq-100 index points, far above 100; a negative, non-numeric or sub-100 one is a unit slip.
As floor_strike, for the upper edge of a range or a 'less' market.

The realised settlement value: the index level the market settled on (KXINX-26OCT06H1600: 7818.93). It is gate G0.1's input against the official close. Null on a settled row means the venue omitted it.
An index level cannot be negative; a negative or non-numeric value is a broken row.
The market's whole-life contracts (volume_fp). Null means the venue omitted it. It is known only after the end of the market: never a feature at a decision.
A contract count cannot be negative.
A market dated at its close cannot be dated after it was acquired; the pack dates an unfinished one at the capture minute.
